data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Calibration analysis alone cannot distinguish genuine reliability gain from compliance-driven confidence, because high box-ticking rates confound confidence with correctness: the discriminating evidence requires cases where compliance is anti-correlated with intuitive correctness.","counterconditions":[{"case":"No counterintuitive-but-correct checklist rules exist in the task domain, so the decoupling is impossible by construction.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The panel's confidence is not measurable or is not reported per-case, making calibration analysis infeasible within the single evaluation.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Counterintuitive cases are so rare that the calibration signal is statistically indistinguishable from noise.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The panel's confidence on counterintuitive cases is driven by group dynamics (e.g., a confident member persuades others) rather than by rule-monitoring, mimicking calibration without genuine meta-monitoring.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The expert's calibration on the same cases is already perfect, leaving no room for the panel to demonstrate superior calibration.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"If the panel's confidence rises with the number of boxes ticked, this is compliance-driven confidence, not genuine calibration. Genuine calibration would require the panel to be more confident on divergence cases it gets right than on divergence cases it gets wrong, independent of how many boxes were ticked. The confound (SCR_002) is that divergence cases where the checklist is right and the panel complies will also have high box-ticking, so compliance rate and correctness are collinear. The decoupling requires cases where the checklist's rule is correct but counterintuitive (high compliance needed, low intuitive confidence) versus cases where it is correct and intuitive (low compliance needed, high intuitive confidence). Only if the panel's confidence tracks correctness rather than box-ticking on the counterintuitive cases can calibration be genuine.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
